00261/head_neck.title: Carboplatin every 3 weeks with head and neck radiotherapy
00261/head_neck.setting: Locally advanced stage III–IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is not appropriate.
00261/head_neck.purpose: Carboplatin is given with radiotherapy to treat locally advanced head and neck cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable. Your team explains the intended chance of cure or long-term control for your diagnosis.
00261/head_neck.schedule: Carboplatin is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 21 days. The head and neck prescription uses AUC 5, a target used with your checked kidney function to calculate the dose. The whole visit includes safety checks, anti-sickness medicines, preparation and observation. Three carboplatin cycles are planned with concurrent radiotherapy. Radiation has a separate appointment calendar; the team coordinates any interruptions or changes.

risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting and fatigue
Kidney, hearing and nerve effects
Infusion allergy, particularly with repeat platinum exposure
Fertility effects and harm to an unborn baby
Sore mouth and throat
Dry mouth, taste and saliva changes
Swallowing or voice problems
Skin reaction in the treated area
Jaw stiffness and dental problems
Some swallowing, saliva or tissue effects can be lasting

00261/head_neck.discussion: Discuss your diagnosis, intent, alternatives, expected benefit and uncertainty, treatment burden, serious or lasting harms, fertility and pregnancy precautions and your priorities. Include blood-count suppression, serious infection and bleeding, nausea/vomiting, allergy, renal dose calculation, hearing and nerve effects, and the separate radiotherapy consent covering mouth, saliva, skin, dental, jaw and swallowing effects. Confirm actual urgent contacts and use teach-back. This draft does not authorise treatment.
limitations: Trial results describe groups; your individual benefit and risks may differ.
Do not transfer survival estimates between different cancer settings, schedules or treatment combinations.
support: This carboplatin regimen has high sickness risk. Take the prescribed prevention and rescue medicines on their written schedule. Call if nausea or vomiting prevents drinking.
Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.
Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.
Ask for speech and language therapy if swallowing or speech is difficult. Use the food textures, exercises and communication support advised for you; a general guide cannot establish safe swallowing.

Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Carboplatin can impair fertility. Do not breastfeed during treatment. The linked Irish product information advises contraception for women during treatment and at least six months afterwards; men should avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least three months afterwards. Confirm the actual product and personal advice.
00261/head_neck.review_status: Source reconciled draft; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

00483/head_neck.title: Nivolumab every 2 weeks for head and neck cancer
00483/head_neck.setting: Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck after platinum treatment; the cancer cannot be treated with curative local therapy and has progressed or returned within six months of the last platinum dose.
00483/head_neck.purpose: Nivolumab aims to control head and neck cancer that has returned or spread, relieve symptoms and help some people live longer. Benefit and side effects are reviewed for you.
00483/head_neck.schedule: Nivolumab is given as 240 mg through a vein over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as an injection under the skin over 3–5 minutes, on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team selects one formulation; these doses are not interchangeable milligram for milligram. Allow extra time for safety checks, preparation and observation. Treatment continues until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable, with individual benefit and safety review. There is no fixed number of cycles in this head and neck treatment course.

risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, hormone glands, skin, heart and nervous system
Infusion or injection reactions
Some effects need steroids, hospital care or long-term hormone replacement
Effects may start after the final dose

00483/head_neck.discussion: Discuss your diagnosis, intent, alternatives, expected benefit and uncertainty, treatment burden, serious or lasting harms, fertility and pregnancy precautions and your priorities. Include immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, skin, glands, heart, muscles, nerves and eyes; infusion or injection reactions; delayed effects; possible high-dose steroid treatment, permanent hormone replacement or permanent treatment stopping. Confirm actual urgent contacts and use teach-back. This draft does not authorise treatment.
limitations: Trial results describe groups; your individual benefit and risks may differ.
Do not transfer survival estimates between different cancer settings, schedules or treatment combinations.
support: Carry your immune alert card during and after nivolumab. Tell any clinician that you have received immunotherapy. Do not restart a held treatment or change prescribed steroids or hormone replacement yourself.
Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.
Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.
Ask for speech and language therapy if swallowing or speech is difficult. Use the food textures, exercises and communication support advised for you; a general guide cannot establish safe swallowing.

Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least five months after the final dose. Tell the team promptly about a possible pregnancy. Do not breastfeed without specific advice from the team.

00455/head_neck.title: Pembrolizumab every 3 weeks for head and neck cancer
00455/head_neck.setting: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with a tumour PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) of at least 1. This indication excludes nasopharyngeal cancer and cancer progressing within six months after curatively intended systemic treatment for locoregionally advanced disease.
00455/head_neck.purpose: Pembrolizumab aims to control head and neck cancer that has returned or spread, relieve symptoms and help some people live longer. Benefit and side effects are reviewed for you.
00455/head_neck.schedule: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks. The whole visit includes safety checks, preparation and observation. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity. After 24 months of sustained response without progression, the team may consider stopping; stopping at 24 months is not automatic.
